question: What does the Maternal Mortality Ratio measure?

options.A: Deaths per 1,000 women of childbearing age
options.B: Total deaths in a specific hospital ward
options.D: Infant deaths compared to maternal deaths

explanation: The Maternal Mortality Ratio is calculated specifically using live births as the denominator to show the risk per pregnancy episode. [learn more](BMP217_U1_T4#BMP217_U1_T4_h1)

question: Why do midwives and researchers study near-miss maternal morbidity cases?

options.A: Patients who survive never experience long-term trauma
options.B: Hospital insurance requires tracking all minor injuries
options.C: Near-miss cases are much easier to legally document
options.D: Survivors share similar complications with women who died

explanation: Looking at women who survived severe emergencies gives healthcare teams valuable clues about how to save others facing identical crises. [learn more](BMP217_U1_T4#BMP217_U1_T4_h1)

question: Which factor directly contributes to the FIRST delay in the Three Delays Model?

options.A: Poor road networks linking villages to the city
options.B: Failure to recognize danger signs at home
options.C: A lack of surgical tools inside the operating theatre
options.D: A shortage of blood bags in the main blood bank

explanation: The first delay happens at the community and household level when family members hesitate or fail to realize a serious emergency is occurring. [learn more](BMP217_U1_T4#BMP217_U1_T4_h2)

question: A woman with severe bleeding waits three hours for a commercial bus because her village has no ambulance. Which delay does this represent?

options.B: Delay in reaching a health facility
options.C: Delay in receiving proper hospital treatment
options.D: Delay in deciding to seek care

explanation: Struggling with transport and distance to get to a clinic falls squarely under the second delay of the model. [learn more](BMP217_U1_T4#BMP217_U1_T4_h2)

question: What is a primary clinical responsibility of a community-based midwife during antenatal visits?

options.A: Screening for conditions like high blood pressure and anemia
options.B: Managing national health policy budgets for maternal care
options.C: Performing complex major abdominal surgeries in village clinics

explanation: Community midwives focus heavily on regular antenatal checkups to catch common, dangerous conditions early before they spiral out of control. [learn more](BMP217_U1_T4#BMP217_U1_T4_h3)

question: How do community midwives help reduce the First Delay in obstetric emergencies?

options.A: By manufacturing emergency blood transfusion kits in the village
options.B: By importing advanced surgical machinery for rural clinics
options.C: By paving roads that connect remote villages to tertiary hospitals
options.D: By educating families to spot danger signs and plan early for birth

explanation: When midwives teach communities what normal versus dangerous symptoms look like, families make the decision to seek help much faster. [learn more](BMP217_U1_T4#BMP217_U1_T4_h3)

question: Which medical service distinguishes a Comprehensive EmOC facility from a Basic EmOC facility?

options.A: Giving oral iron supplements during antenatal care

explanation: Only Comprehensive EmOC (CEmOC) facilities are equipped and staffed to carry out blood transfusions and major surgeries like caesarean sections. [learn more](BMP217_U1_T4#BMP217_U1_T4_h4)

question: Why is relying solely on community-based primary prevention insufficient to eliminate maternal deaths?

options.A: Traditional birth attendants solve all surgical problems locally
options.B: Unpredictable life-threatening complications will still occur during childbirth
options.C: Midwives are legally prohibited from managing normal deliveries alone
options.D: Pregnant women in rural areas refuse to attend community health talks

explanation: Some severe obstetric emergencies, such as sudden hemorrhage or obstructed labor, happen without warning and require advanced facility-based surgery. [learn more](BMP217_U1_T4#BMP217_U1_T4_h4)

question: What is the primary goal of a Maternal Death Surveillance and Response (MDSR) system?

options.A: To investigate every maternal death and implement corrective local actions
options.B: To calculate exact tax rates for families living in rural communities
options.C: To restrict pregnant women from traveling far away from home
options.D: To punish healthcare workers who make clinical mistakes in surgery

explanation: MDSR is designed to track and learn from every loss of life so the health system can fix systemic flaws and prevent future tragedies. [learn more](BMP217_U1_T4#BMP217_U1_T4_h5)

question: What happens when a country has weak vital registration and poor civil recording systems?

options.A: Pregnant women completely stop visiting modern health facilities
options.B: Midwives stop keeping records of antenatal clinic attendees
options.C: Maternal deaths are underreported and resource planning is difficult
options.D: Hospitals receive too much funding for emergency blood supplies

explanation: Without accurate data on births and deaths, policymakers cannot target funding or interventions where they are needed most. [learn more](BMP217_U1_T4#BMP217_U1_T4_h5)
